tob-10091: Scottish preacher Alexander Whyte offers a warm tribute to Teresa of Ávila, the sixteenth-century Spanish nun and mystic. He recounts her work reforming the Carmelite order and her writings on prayer, which describe the soul’s ascent to God in vivid stages. Whyte, himself a beloved Protestant minister, wrote for readers of all faiths who want to know this remarkable woman.
tob-10791: Thomas Thomson, a pioneering chemistry professor at Glasgow, wrote one of the first histories of his science. This first volume covers the subject from its alchemical beginnings through the early modern founders of chemistry. Thomson knew many of the figures he describes, giving his account the flavor of a witness rather than a distant historian.
tob-4291: The first volume of Frazer’s Golden Bough opens his vast hunt through wonder-working and worship — Nemi’s priest, the dying god, the hedge of taboo round kings. His way of heaping witness on witness built an empire of proof. The volume sets the stage for comparative faith’s most weighty work.
tob-0191: Max Muller’s Upanishads — from the Sacred Books of the East — give the forest talks on the All-One and the Self that crown Vedic thought. His trail-blazing Victorian scholarship opened Indian wisdom to the West. The volumes stay landmarks of rendering.
tob-4191: Hermann Oldenberg’s 1879 Dipavamsa gives old Ceylon’s Buddhist year-book — the isle’s turning to the faith and the tale of its kings. His edition and rendering opened Pali story-books to the western world. The text is the oldest Buddhist history to survive.
cia-0000105891: From April 1965, a report estimating that Indonesian Communist Party activity would peak with mass action against the United States. The PKI was the world's largest non-ruling communist party, and Washington feared it was closing in on power. The estimate proved tragically wrong about the direction of events: the army, not the communists, would strike first.
cia-0000107291: From June 1991, a report on diplomats' reactions to a photograph said to show a living American missing in action. Photos claiming to show live MIAs surfaced regularly and were usually debunked, but each one demanded investigation. The entry shows the care — and the skepticism — with which such claims were handled.
cia-0000107391: An October 1975 study of how deeply the Soviet Union depended on space systems — satellites for spying, communications, and guiding weapons. Space had become a battlefield without soldiers, and understanding the enemy's orbital habits was vital. The report shows the CIA mapping a new dimension of the arms race a decade into the space age.
cia-0000126891: A November 1970 weekly review on Vietnam, covering fallout from the Son Tay raid — part of the title deleted. The daring American raid on a POW camp found it empty, but shook Hanoi. The document assesses the aftermath: a failed rescue that still sent a message.
cia-0000132191: Situation Report 508: France and the European Community smoothing relations with Israel — the truncated title suggests the rest. Keeping Israel out of the war was the coalition's great diplomatic project. The document tracks the courtship: Europe reassuring Jerusalem while Scuds fell.
cia-0000132291: Situation Report 600: Iraqis remaining defiant — the truncated title suggests the political developments. Six hundred daily reports into the crisis, Baghdad still talked tough. The document is defiance numbered: the six-hundredth installment of a war's diary.
cia-0000132491: An April 1960 report, its title carrying the archive's typo, on bloc economic relations with Cuba: the Soviet trade pact, plus satellite and Chinese activity. The communist world's checkbooks were opening for Havana. The document follows the money: the revolution, financed.
cia-0000135291: An estimated 1983 document on a world assembly for peace and life against nuclear war — the archive's title is garbled. The anti-nuclear movement was peaking as the arms race raged. The document is the assembly: the movement, gathered — through a mangled title.

cia-0000135991: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with implementation instructions for SYNCARP materials — the archive's spelling says instuctions, the truncated title cuts off the rest. The project moved from planning to doing. The entry is the instruction: the materials, deployed.

cia-0000140391: A 1954 document — author deleted — with comments on the proposal to use hypnotized couriers. The mind-controlled messenger. The document is the proposal: the courier, hypnotized.

arxiv-2605-08891: Autoencoders compress data into compact inner representations, but those representations are usually inscrutable. Thomas Dooms, Ward Gauderis, Geraint Wiggins, and Jose Oramas show that bilinear autoencoders uncover interpretable manifolds — inner structures a human can actually read. The 2026 paper is representation learning with the hood open.
arxiv-2605-08991: Rating systems — chess Elo, product stars — often lean on heuristic estimation methods whose reliability is folk wisdom. Jacek Szybowski, Konrad Kułakowski, and Jiri Mazurek pin down sufficient conditions for one such heuristic rating estimation method to be safely applied. The 2026 paper turns a rule of thumb into a theorem with boundaries.
arxiv-2605-09191: Laser-driven fusion accelerates protons inside solid targets, and knowing their energies is crucial. Hiroki Matsubara, Ryunosuke Takizawa, Yuga Karaki, and colleagues probe in-solid proton energy distributions using nuclear activation diagnostics. The 2026 paper is fusion diagnostics: reading the blast's fingerprints.
arxiv-2605-09291: Flow models generate discretely — tokens, not pixels — and training them with policy optimization needs rate awareness. Zhengyan Wan, Yidong Ouyang, Panwen Hu, and Qiang Sun propose dFlowGRPO: rate-aware policy optimization for discrete flow models. The 2026 paper tunes the learning to the generation's pace.
arxiv-2605-09391: Linear probes read concepts out of a model's activations, and persona coordinates — axes defined by personalities — might organize them better. Prasad Mahadik and Adrians Skapars ask whether probes generalize better there. The 2026 paper is an interpretability experiment with a clever coordinate system.
arxiv-2605-09491: Category theory promises elegant abstractions for message-passing programs, but programmers need a language, not a textbook. Daniel Kiyoshi Hashimoto, Alexanna Little Berg, and colleagues propose CaMPL, the categorical message passing language. The 2026 paper brings categorical ideas down to code.
arxiv-2605-09591: Segmentation models outline objects beautifully — but do they know what a dog is? Shuang Liang, Zeqing Wang, Yuxian Li, and colleagues ask whether segmentation models understand what they segment, from pixels to concepts. The 2026 paper probes the meaning behind the masks.
arxiv-2605-09691: Drugs move through body compartments in complex dynamics that quantum circuits might one day simulate efficiently. Isshaan Singh and Nandan Patel explore variational quantum algorithms for nonlinear mixed-effects population pharmacokinetics. The 2026 paper is quantum computing meets serious drug modeling.
arxiv-2605-09791: How vital is a group — its marginal contribution to the whole coalition? Natalia Kucharczuk and Oskar Skibski axiomatize group vitality indices and provide efficient algorithms to compute them in practice. The 2026 paper is cooperative game theory made fully operational at last.
arxiv-2605-09891: Floating car data, traffic camera observations, and network flow analysis each see traffic differently; together they estimate volume. Antonina Kosikova, Mehmet Kerem Turkcan, Ahmed Darrat, and colleagues harness all three. The 2026 paper is smart traffic estimation from fused sensor signals.
arxiv-2605-09991: Optimizers shape the connectivity of loss landscapes; mode connectivity induced by optimizers, from AdamW to Muon. Fangzhao Zhang, Sungyoon Kim, Erica Zhang, and colleagues trace the effect. The 2026 paper is optimization theory on how training choices connect minima. It connects minima across optimizers.
plos-pone-0003391: Gut-disease researchers connected a gene variant to broken cleanup in this 2008 paper. Crohn's disease risk had been tied to ATG16L1, but the mechanism was unclear. The team showed the variant cripples autophagy, the cell's self-cleaning system, against an invading intracellular pathogen, suggesting Crohn's patients may struggle to clear microbes hiding inside their own cells.
plos-pone-0003491: Methodologists delivered an unexpected verdict on trial quality in this 2008 review. African HIV/AIDS trials were more likely than others to report solid randomization and concealed treatment assignment, the bedrock of unbiased trials. The finding challenges assumptions about where rigorous clinical research happens and praises the standards African trial teams actually met.
plos-pone-0003591: Olfaction researchers found genes outlasting diet in mouse smell in this 2008 paper. Each mouse carries a unique genetically based odor signature, and the team showed those signatures persist even when diets change. The finding means individual recognition by smell is written in DNA, not in dinner.
plos-pone-0003691: In 2008, Peck, Smeeth, and Whittaker pooled the genetics of bleeding strokes. Single studies of haemorrhagic stroke, subarachnoid bleeding, and ruptured brain aneurysms were too small to crack the genetics alone. Their meta-analysis combined candidate-gene data to give the field its first solid footing.
plos-pone-0003791: Sussan, Jun, and Thimmulappa found an antioxidant switch feeding artery plaques in this 2008 mouse paper. Knocking out Nrf2, a master inducer of antioxidant defenses, paradoxically eased ApoE-driven atherosclerosis. The surprise shows oxidative stress pathways pulling double duty in heart disease.
plos-pone-0003891: A 2008 paper proposed a living lab for germs meeting new hosts. Gopalan and Ausubel outlined a metasystem of model organisms to study emerging host-microbe adaptations. The framework anticipates the new microbial partnerships industrialization keeps creating.
plos-pone-0003991: In 2008, Mullen, Bosse, and Nair found a bacterial protein with two talents. The ComE1 protein of Pasteurella multocida both grips fibronectin and grabs DNA. The double duty may help the pathogen stick to hosts and swap genes. The discovery reveals a true multitasker at work in the Pasteurellaceae bacterial family.
plos-pone-0004091: In 2008, Smith, Willan, and Warr deleted a gene and watched mice breed fine. The Maestro gene proved unnecessary for normal sexual development and fertility. Male and female mice grew up and reproduced without it. The knockout closes one suspect in gonad formation.
plos-pone-0004191: In 2009, Sawka, Goldstein, and Brierley asked survivors how treatment felt. Thyroid cancer patients recalled radioactive iodine therapy's impact on their lives. The post-surgical treatment left mixed memories. The patient voices guide gentler care. The study puts lived experience beside survival statistics.
plos-pone-0004291: In 2009, Mercer and Wevrick found a missing gene dimming mouse fertility. Losing Magel2, a Prader-Willi-linked gene, impaired mouse reproduction. The gene's absence dulled reproductive function. The mouse model clarifies the syndrome's reach. The work separates Magel2's role from neighboring genes.
plos-pone-0358491: Batteries, fuel cells, and many industrial processes depend on how charged particles, called ions, move through liquids. This chemistry paper offers a simplified theory for predicting when positive and negative ions cling together into pairs inside electrolyte mixtures. A workable model lets engineers design better batteries and chemical processes without running a costly experiment for every new mixture.
plos-pone-0358591: Zebrafish are genetics workhorses, and every experiment starts with DNA extraction. This paper presented a rapid, cost-effective Chelex-100 resin method for pulling genomic DNA from adult zebrafish tissues. The cheap, fast protocol lowers the barrier for fish genetics labs everywhere.
plos-pone-0347591: What really drives PM2.5 pollution — the weather or the landscape? This climate-stratified machine learning assessment found that geographic controls dominate meteorological factors. The finding reframes pollution policy: where you are matters more than what the sky is doing.
plos-pone-0356491: Some heart blocks demand pacemakers — and some of the risks leading there can be modified. This cohort study identified modifiable predictors of atrioventricular block warranting a pacemaker. The predictors hand cardiologists concrete prevention targets instead of waiting for the block to arrive.
plos-pone-0357791: Late preterm babies — born just a few weeks early — need carefully tuned nutrition to thrive. This study examined how adherence to nutrition guidelines and fortification of feeds affect the growth of late preterm neonates. The findings help neonatal units optimize feeding for these vulnerable infants.
plos-pone-0357291: Predicting who will develop lung cancer from lifestyle and clinical data could save lives through earlier screening. This paper built interpretable ensemble models for lung cancer risk prediction. The transparent models don’t just predict — they show exactly which factors drive each person’s risk.
plos-pone-0356891: Adolescent tobacco use is rising across Sub-Saharan Africa — largely unmeasured until now. This comparative analysis of national cross-sectional surveys across three countries measured prevalence and associated factors. The data give public health officials the evidence base for youth-targeted prevention.
plos-pone-0357091: Youth experiencing homelessness face appalling rates of sex trafficking. This cross-sectional study measured the prevalence and characteristics of trafficking among homeless youth. The stark numbers demand targeted intervention for some of society’s most invisible victims.
plos-pone-0356791: Young Chinese physicians endure standardized training’s crushing pressures — but how do they cope? This paper investigated perceived stress, depression, and their interrelationships among these doctors. The findings expose a mental health crisis in white coats and point to where support must go.
plos-pone-0356691: Diabetic kidney disease and Parkinson’s disease seem worlds apart — yet their immune signatures may converge. This multimodal analysis suggested partial IRF8/TLR7-associated myeloid transcriptional convergence between the two. The shared immune program hints at common therapeutic targets across seemingly unrelated diseases.
plos-pone-0355191: Watching neuropeptides move in a living worm could unlock neurobiology’s secrets. This paper achieved neuropeptide visualization using split GFP in live C. elegans. The glowing-peptide technique lets scientists watch chemical signaling unfold in real time inside a transparent, living animal.
plos-pone-0352591: Rocks with crossing fractures behave unpredictably under repeated loading. This paper studied the mechanical properties of rock with cross fractures under biaxial compression with cyclic loading and unloading. The findings help engineers predict how fractured rock masses will respond to the stresses of mining and tunneling.
plos-pone-0355691: Sand mining in Ghana operates in a legal gray zone — and stakeholders’ attitudes decide whether laws matter. This paper analyzed actors’ attitudes toward the legal institutional framework for sand mining in two local government areas. The findings expose why regulations fail on the ground — and what might make them stick.
plos-pone-0355491: Primary care doctors eyeing large language models — with hope and wariness — deserve systematic study. This qualitative research protocol leverages technology acceptance theory to understand their perceptions of LLM adoption. The planned research will reveal what would make physicians actually trust AI in the exam room.
plos-pone-0353391: Can people tell when a moral judgment comes from an AI — and does the source change their agreement? This moral Turing test examined how belief and source shape detection of and agreement with LLM judgments. The findings probe the unsettling frontier where machine morality meets human conscience.
plos-pone-0355391: Tanzania’s school feeding program — does it genuinely improve children’s diets? This Kisarawe district study examined implementation and its effect on dietary adequacy among primary schoolers. The findings test whether the meals on offer translate into the nutrition growing bodies need.
plos-pone-0343191: Parkinson’s severity might be trackable through speech — personalized and uncertainty-aware. This paper developed uncertainty-aware personalized estimation of disease severity from longitudinal speech data. The voice-based monitoring promises objective tracking of a disease that currently relies on subjective rating scales.
europmc-pmc2796391: The staph germ causes grave illness across Europe, but its strains vary by place. This 2010 study maps which types rule in each country, using DNA typing. The map lets clinics brace for drug-proof strains and flare-ups. It ranks among the biggest joint surveys of serious staph ever done.
europmc-pmc2814091: Stem cells grown in the lab for months may not stay the same, and this 2010 paper tracks what changes. The authors measure DNA methylation patterns in human mesenchymal stromal cells during long-term culture and aging. They find the chemical marks on DNA shift over time. The work warns that cultured cells drift, which matters for therapies built on them.
europmc-pmc2820091: Receptors usually pass signals into cells, but this 2010 paper reveals one that works as a molecular vacuum cleaner. The authors show the receptor CXCR7 scavenges the signaling proteins CXCL12 and CXCL11, soaking them up to shape their gradients. This cleanup role changes how immune cells navigate. The discovery added a new trick to the immune system's playbook.
europmc-pmc2928191: Blood vessel walls leak by rules, and this 2010 paper measures them. The author sets physiologic upper limits of pore size for different capillary types and revisits the dual pore theory of microvascular permeability. Their numbers ground drug delivery design. The work refined a classic theory.
europmc-pmc2936891: Brain pipes lean on helper cells called pericytes. This 2010 paper tracks a key signal receiver on pericytes in mice with working and broken signaling. The authors clarify how vessels get support. Their findings matter for stroke and dementia care. The work may guide new vessel-protecting drugs.
europmc-pmc3026691: Trial outcomes need choosing well. This 2011 paper shows how expert rounds can pick what trials should measure. The authors' recommendations guide trial designers. Their work shaped reporting standards. Patients' voices now join the expert panels. Core outcome sets spread after this push.
europmc-pmc3049591: A simple blood score predicts cancer survival. This 2011 Glasgow study shows an inflammation-based score forecasts survival across tumor types. The authors validate the score. Their work aids cancer doctors. Two cheap blood tests feed the score. High scores flag patients needing closer watch.
europmc-pmc3084991: Liver cancer care got an update. This 2011 liver-society paper updates how doctors manage hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors' guidelines shape care. Their work standardized treatment. Staging scans now drive every decision. Transplant rules got clearer cutoffs. The update is cited in every liver unit.
europmc-pmc6517691: Your gut's bacterial community shifts as you age, and men and women host different mixes - but the details were fuzzy. Analyzing three large adult cohorts across four regions, researchers mapped how microbial diversity rises and falls with age in each sex. The patterns give scientists a baseline for asking whether age- and sex-specific gut profiles influence health and disease.
europmc-pmc6687891: Baker's yeast is biology's favorite test tube - and now it has a consensus wiring diagram. Yeast8 is a community-curated genome-scale metabolic model of S. cerevisiae, with an ecosystem of tools for probing cellular metabolism. The shared resource lets researchers simulate the cell before touching a pipette.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1091: The EPA's cleanup of downtown towers after 9/11 drew GAO's skeptical eye in 2007. Its test-and-clean program for the World Trade Center zone raised flags the report says needed answers. The findings press for better proof that the air and dust where New Yorkers lived and worked were truly safe.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-691: NASA's business software was thinking small in 2007 — GAO's report says the space agency had to weigh agency-wide needs to get its money's worth. The findings push for enterprise thinking over fiefdom buying. Rockets may fly solo, the report argues, but their back office should not.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-791: Old rules deserved second looks in 2007 — GAO's report says Washington could do better at reviewing whether regulations still earned their keep. The findings pitch retrospective review as good government hygiene. The report's motto: rules should have to re-audition for their jobs.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-591: The Great Lakes' beaches were getting graded in 2007 — GAO's report says the EPA and states had moved on the beach-health law, with more to do. The findings track the cleanup. The report's standard: the world's largest freshwater shores deserve swimmable water.
gao-gaoreports-b-299291: MCS Portable Restroom Service took its March 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest. Even portable-toilet contracts get the full bid-law treatment.
openalex-w7204754091: Clean water and sewers shape public health, yet Brazil's Amazon region lags far behind. This comparative study looks at two cities in eastern Amazonia, Castanhal and Maraba, measuring sanitation, health, and income side by side. The authors document deep gaps within a single state. A data-driven portrait of how unequal basic services translate into unequal health.
openalex-w4409453391: Crystal surfaces can host strange electronic states. This theory paper models electron bands on different faces of a cubic lattice with eg orbitals, finding a flat surface state tied to an octupole moment. The authors mapped the band structures. A condensed-matter study of surfaces with exotic character.
openalex-w7172334291: Seeing whole organs in 3D takes clever optics. This paper presents a do-it-yourself light-sheet microscope for four-color volumetric imaging of intact specimens. The authors extended the design for complex samples. An imaging-methods paper democratizing deep tissue views.
openalex-w4406942591: Eczema's maddening itch starts deep in the skin. This review covers why atopic dermatitis itches so badly: broken skin walls plus haywire immune signals. The authors untangled the itch pathway step by step. A skin review of why scratching never brings relief.
pmc-13469691: A 2026 microbiology paper characterizing the natural AmpC beta-lactamase of Escherichia marmotae — an enzyme that breaks down antibiotics — and measuring how it reduces the bacteria's susceptibility to cefiderocol, a last-resort drug. Mapping the resistance helps doctors anticipate which antibiotics will still work.
pmc-13521291: A 2026 plant genetics paper showing that a cysteine-rich receptor-like kinase and MADS-box genes jointly trigger programmed cell death that kills off the top spikelets of wheat ears. This degeneration caps how many grains each wheat head can make. Understanding the control circuit opens a path to fuller ears and higher yields.
pmc-13397391: This 2026 oncology paper linked systemic inflammation to risk of blood clots, mortality, and treatment response in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Inflammation markers may flag who needs clot prevention and who will respond. The findings add a practical layer to immunotherapy care.
pmc-13499191: In this 2026 drug development paper, researchers built a PBD dimer-containing antibody-drug conjugate targeting CCRL2 for high-risk MDS/AML, including TP53-mutated disease. The ultra-potent payload aims at a marker of the worst-prognosis leukemias. The preclinical work is the first step.
pmc-13424091: A 2026 paper on qubit-efficient quantum intrusion detection using dual-parameter encoding and multi-metric calibration. Quantum cybersecurity is emerging. The encoding scheme is the contribution.
pmc-13523791: A 2026 optics paper on step-scan interferometry for high-fidelity hyperspectral nanoscopy. The technique sharpened nanoscale spectral imaging. The interferometry is the advance.
pmc-13492991: A 2026 qualitative paper on patients' experience of prescribed exercise in musculoskeletal physiotherapy — the how and why of exercise prescription. The patients' voices were centered. The experience is the data.
pmc-13488391: In this 2026 materials paper, hydrogenation trapped the excess electron of FeB-type CeSi — forming ferromagnetic hydrides. The hydrides' magnetism was the prize. The trapping is the physics.
pmc-13488491: This 2026 chemistry paper synthesized binaphthol-based macrocycles as dual metal cation chemosensors — with spectroscopic characterization and molecular dynamics insights (the title is truncated). The sensors detected two metals. The macrocycles are the achievement.
pmc-13462891: A 2026 plant pathology paper on a novel SYBR Green real-time PCR detection marker for Xanthomonas fragariae in strawberry plants. The bacterial threat was detectable. The marker is the diagnostic.
pmc-13449891: A 2026 life cycle assessment quantifying sustainability of alternative methanol production pathways — biomass-to-methanol, waste-to-methanol, or power-to-X (the title is truncated). The green methanol routes were compared. The quantifying is the policy input.
pmc-13356891: A 2026 UK feasibility study of an adapted participatory group program for caregivers of children with complex neurodisability (the title is truncated). The caregiver program was piloted. The feasibility is the result.
pmc-13436691: This 2026 deep learning paper captured position-specific effects of plant regulatory sequences and suggested genes under complex regulation. The AI decoded the plant promoters. The capturing is the advance.
pmc-13493191: A 2026 commentary asking whether clonal haematopoiesis is the missing link between lupus and cardiovascular disease. The question connects the fields. The commentary is the hypothesis.
pmc-13472891: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of dual orexin receptor antagonists for chronic insomnia in elderly adults. The sleep drugs' geriatric evidence was pooled. The review guides prescribing.
pmc-13599191: In this 2026 case report, locally advanced gastric adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation and PD-L1 positivity was successfully managed non-surgically (the title is truncated). The chemo-immunotherapy avoided the knife. The management is the hope.
pmc-13439991: A 2026 multi-protocol study pooling quantitative MRI data on healthy subcortical aging. The brain aging data were harmonized. The pooling is the normative resource.
pmc-13454991: A 2026 review on advances in miR-200c regulation of apoptosis, pyroptosis, and autophagy in disease. The microRNA's cell death roles were surveyed. The review is the synthesis.
pmc-13586591: A 2026 AI paper introducing a novel chaos-inspired artificial intelligence model for keratoconus prediction. The chaotic dynamics served the eye disease prediction. The model is the diagnostic tool.
pmc-13526791: In this 2026 paper, accurate, transferable, and verifiable machine-learned interatomic potentials for layered materials were developed. The AI force fields were trustworthy. The verifiability is the advance.
pmc-13514991: A 2026 retrospective study predicting Ki-67 expression in esophageal cancer patients based on delta radiomics. The imaging AI forecasted the proliferation marker. The predicting aids oncology.
pmc-13467391: A 2026 pilot study with longitudinal exploratory analysis of salivary microbiota profiles in oral squamous cell carcinoma patients before and after surgery. The mouth's microbes shifted with treatment. The profiles are the preliminary data.
pmc-13520891: In this 2026 response letter, the authors replied to correspondence regarding their article on infection outbreaks caused by carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (the title is truncated). The scholarly exchange continues. The response is the record.
pmc-13515591: A 2026 materials paper on construction and properties of SPI/PLA-PCL composite coating on pure titanium surface. The bio-composite coating was characterized. The properties serve implant design.
pmc-13512591: A 2026 Beijing cross-sectional study of ACTN3, MTHFR, and MTRR polymorphism distribution in 564 school-aged children. The gene variants' prevalence was mapped. The distribution is the population data.
pmc-13461791: A 2026 paper developing and validating the inclusive sport attitudes scale for pre-service sport professionals (ISA-PS). The attitudes measure was validated. The scale serves sport education.
pmc-13417991: In this 2026 materials paper, fluorine substitution's influence was examined in naphthalenediimide-bithiophene-based n-type conjugated polymers for organic electrochemical transistors (the title is truncated). The fluorination tuned the polymers. The influence is the materials design rule.
pmc-13421491: In this 2026 paper, genomic profiling identified actionable DNA-repair defects in a new cervical cancer model. The model's vulnerabilities were mapped. The identifying guides targeted therapy.
arxiv-2606-16191: Sorting malware into families helps defenders recognize new variants quickly. This paper applies quantum kernel methods — machine learning enhanced by quantum-computing ideas — to classify malware at scale. It explores whether quantum techniques can keep up with the growing flood of malicious software samples hitting security teams.
arxiv-2606-16291: Trust no span till the code twin nods. This paper builds a rich code twin of a full-size test bridge and wrings out how it bends, shakes, and bears weight. Span pros use such twins to check their sums earn real trust.
arxiv-2606-16691: When heavy quarks are born in particle collisions, they dress themselves in other quarks — "hadronization." The LHCb collaboration finds that in high-multiplicity collisions, this dressing process changes. The paper reports the measurement for particle physicists studying how quarks become the matter we see.
arxiv-2606-16891: Federated learning trains AI across devices without sharing raw data — but devices must still send messages. This paper taxonomizes those messages: beyond weights and gradients, what else flies across the wire? It is for federated learning researchers. Know the mail, trim the mail.
